description: An aerial or satellite image presented as a False-Colour Infrared (FCIR) composite, showing a landscape near Malaga, Spain. The image displays a river flowing through the top-left, areas of active vegetation appearing in vibrant red, and lighter brown/grey areas representing bare earth or sparse vegetation. On the right, a structured urban area with a grid-like street pattern and buildings is visible. In the central-left portion of the image, an area outlined in light cyan is labelled with the code "1320". This area appears as mottled light brown/grey, indicating bare ground or land with secondary rural vegetation, consistent with the definition of "Land without current use." This classification (1320) refers to areas in a transitional state, such as wasteland, former industrial areas ("brownfields"), or undeveloped gaps within or near urban areas ("greenfields"), without visible construction or maintenance, but also not undisturbed natural vegetation. The image is credited to M. Palacios.
